title: First recursive descent branch
statement: Let $E,s,w,i\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{orc}$ be a Boolean oracle on four indices and Boolean words, let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $\mathrm{st}$ be a register state. Assume $s\leq w$, $i+1\leq w$, the recursive call property holds at level $i$, the state satisfies the level-$(i+1)$ invariant with parameters $s,w$, and its midpoint register $M$ is strictly less than $2^w$. Then there is an $M_1\leq 2^w$ such that, starting at the midpoint-search loop with this state, the machine reaches the phase-1 push site if the level-$i$ reachability predicate holds from the source code $U$ to the current midpoint $M$, and otherwise reaches the phase-0 failure site. At the end, the target register is the old midpoint, the popped-endpoint register is the old target, and the midpoint register is $M_1$; throughout the run all configurations satisfy the guard bounding every register by $2^{w^2}$ and requiring valid instructions.
